title: WPSS/1733/2014 of Nutan Mishra Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1733 of 2014
Nutan Misra Ö Petitioner
 Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. Kishore Kumar, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Hariya, Standing Counsel, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
1. Heard Mr. Kishore Kumar, learned counsel for the
petitioner, Mr. Pradeep Hariya, Standing Counsel for the State
of Uttarakhand and perused the record.
2. By means of the present writ petition, petitioner has
sought following reliefs:-
i) Issue writ rule or direction in the nature of
mandamus declaring the condition inserted in the
amended rules known as Uttarakhand Recruitment to
Services (Age Limit) (First Amendment) Rules, 2014 as
unreasonable and ultravires to the constitution of India so
far as it put restriction for enhancement of age limit on
the existing process of recruitment pursuant to the
advertisement in question after calling the entire records.
ii) Issue writ rule or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing to the respondents to accept the
candidature of the petitioner for the post of Assistant
Teacher Primary pursuant to advertisement and her
application dated 21.02.2014, had it been the impugned
condition by not allowing the enhancement of age to the
existing advertisement was never in existence.
iii) Issue a writ rule or direction in the nature of
mandamus to declare the petitioner for enhancement of
age at par to the other S.C./S.T. and O.B.C. category of
persons keeping in view her status as Socially Backward
being a lady and to allow her the aforesaid benefits of age
relaxation at par to the aforesaid categories of employees
and further to consider her case for age relaxation as per
rules in vogue.
iv) Issue a writ rule or direction appropriate in nature
by awarding suitable damages to the petitioner for the
constitutional torts of the respondents as highlighted in
the body of the petition.
3. Case of the petitioner in nutshell is that she
responded to an advertisement dated 01.02.2014 issued by

2
respondent No. 2 ñ Director, Elementary Education,
Uttarakhand, whereby applications were invited from eligible
candidates for appointment as Assistant Teacher in
Government Primary Schools. According to the advertisement,
any candidate, who had not completed 40 years of age as on
01.07.2013 was eligible to apply, while petitioner had
completed 40 years of age much earlier on 21.03.2013. It is
the case of petitioner that a news report was published on
20.02.2014 stating that State Cabinet has taken a decision to
enhance maximum age limit for employment under the State
from 40 years to 42 years in respect of candidates belonging to
General category. In view of the said news report, petitioner
submitted her application with the legitimate expectation that
her claim would be considered on merit. Thereafter on
25.02.2014, a notification was issued by the State Government,
whereby Uttarakhand Recruitment to Services (Age Limit)
Rules, 2014 were amended. By the said amendment, upper
age limit for recruitment to State services was increased from
40 years to 42 years. However, proviso was also added therein
that amendment will not apply where the vacancies have
already been advertised. This proviso has been challenged in
the writ petition on various grounds.
4. This Court vide order dated 29.09.2016 had directed
that one post of Assistant Teacher, Primary School shall be
kept vacant.
5. During the course of argument, learned counsel for
the petitioner gave up challenge to the Rules i.e. Uttarakhand
Recruitment to Services (Age Limit)(First Amendment) Rules,
2014 and he limits his argument to the extent that there are
Statutory Rules known as ìUttarakhand Public Service
(Relaxation in age Limit for recruitment) Rules, 2003î, which
were notified on 28.02.2003 and Rule 3 thereof enables the
State Government to grant relaxation in upper age limit for

3
appointment to public services. Now, learned counsel for the
petitioner confines his prayer and submits that the Competent
Authority be directed to consider petitionerís claim for age
relaxation and pass appropriate order.
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of with
liberty to the petitioner to make a representation, raising all his
contentions, to the State Government within two weeks from
today. If such a representation is made, the Competent
Authority shall consider petitionerís claim for relaxation in
upper age limit in terms of Rule 3 of the aforesaid Rules and
pass a speaking order, in accordance with law, within a period
of six weeks thereafter.
(Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
05.09.2017
Aswal
